A4 says 'SQLCipher everywhere' with no residual, while storage.encrypt=false is a supported option

14 puts heavy parsers in a sandboxed parse worker; 04 says the worker uses 'the ext-host OS sandbox' (owned by nm-lua-sandbox, 12:15), but nm-ingest may not depend on nm-lua-sandbox (01:179); and the ext-host seccomp filter denies execve (12:18) while the worker falls back to pdftotext (04:376)
audit example uses op_group 'op_01JA…', the same op_ prefix as individual op IDs, though OpGroupId is a distinct type

One writer actor 'owns the only read-write connection to each file', yet nm-search 'owns the frecency table's writes through its own short transactions' (also plan.md:577 WP-49). sender_frecency is in index.db (03:377).

03 §2 places blobs.db under nm-store (section title, writer per file, weekly sweep, view copies); README and plan give blobs.db, BlobStore, the sweep and the runtime view-copy manager to nm-blobs. 03 never names nm-blobs or BlobStore.

Same ownership conflict for the sweep and tmpfs view copies: 03 describes them in nm-store's section with no owner; plan WP-50 assigns them to nm-blobs; 11:10 attributes view/ paths to attachment.fetch (nm-attach).
SafeText doc says it is safe for 'a log line'; the logging owner drops subject/text/address fields unless a redaction-safe newtype, and logs hold IDs, not content.

SafeText doc says it is safe for 'an LLM envelope'; the classifier inserts a redaction step before DecisionRequest, and the Redactor fix requires DecisionRequest to accept only RedactedText. Terminal safety is being presented as egress safety.

SearchIndex is claimed swappable for tantivy, but FTS rows are written by nm-store's writer via Store::index_text in the same transaction; a tantivy SearchIndex would get no writes through its own port (swap test fails).
render.show_invisible is used here but absent from 13's config example, which claims to show every section with defaults.
Cross-ref says the first-run cost estimate is in 06 §8; it is in 06 §7 (line 180). 06 §8 is 'Classify once'.
UUIDv7 kinds listed as ops, jobs, approvals, sessions (op_ prefix only); 07 shows an undo_ prefixed ID that is not listed.

Classification redaction is a RedactionLevel enum (13: metadata|standard|full under classify.redaction), while 06's table names a `privacy.redaction` field, 12/13 add a separate mcp.redaction, and the Redactor fix introduces privacy.detectors. Ownership of the redaction keys is split.
